title: Project Policy
description: What a specific project is held to. The policy selects and configures rules; it never redefines them. Rule identity and metadata belong to the catalog in rules/, and evidence belongs to the evaluator. Nothing in this document asserts compliance — what a project actually meets is the result of `standards evaluate`.

standardVersion.description: The framework version this project is evaluated against. A version that cannot be resolved is a configuration error, not a compliance failure, and exits 2.

project.description: Project identity, carried into the evaluator's output so a report can be attributed.

rules.description: Per-rule level. A rule absent here takes its catalog level. A policy may raise an obligation and may never lower one: setting a rule below its catalog level is a weakening of the standard and is reported as an integrity violation.

applicability.description: Whether each rule's SUBJECT exists in this project at all. Distinct from an exception, and the two must never collapse into one mechanism: not-applicable means the rule has nothing to bite on here; an exception means the rule applies and the project knowingly does not satisfy it. Only the second needs an approver and an expiry.

exceptions.description: Approved, time-bounded waivers of rules that DO apply. An exception against a non-exemptible rule is rejected rather than honoured, and rejection is checked before expiry so a lapsed non-exemptible waiver does not report as merely expired.

attestations.description: Recorded human judgement for rules no mechanism can establish from repository text. An attestation never overrides an automated finding; where a check observed a violation, an approving attestation is reported as contradicted and the rule still fails.

ruleId.description: Canonical rule identity, `category.kebab-case-name`. There is no alias mechanism: any other spelling is rejected here rather than quietly accepted, because a vocabulary allowed to fork is one that will need reconciling later.

note.description: Why this project set the rule as it did.

reason.description: Required, and required to be substantive. A not-applicable declaration with no reason is indistinguishable from an oversight, which is exactly what declaring it is meant to prevent.

reviewedAt.description: When a human last confirmed this. Paired with an equivalent pattern because `format` is an annotation and is not validated.

revisitWhen.description: The event that would make this determination wrong. Reported by `standards status` alongside the mechanical revisit triggers.

reason.description: Why this project knowingly does not satisfy an applicable rule.

approvedBy.description: Who accepted the risk. An exception with no approver is a mute button.

expires.description: After this date the waiver stops waiving and the rule fails again.

reference.description: A decision record or ticket where the approval is documented.

status.description: A recorded rejection is a failure, not silence. Both outcomes are worth writing down.

evidence.description: What the reviewer examined and what they found. Required, because an attestation without it is an assertion rather than evidence.

expires.description: After this date the attestation stops establishing the rule, which returns to not-evaluated rather than failing.

reviewedAgainst.description: What the reviewer actually looked at. Supplying a digest is what makes the attestation expire on its own when the reviewed material changes — the difference between a review and a permanent approval.

digest.description: Digest over the contents of `paths`, as printed by `standards evaluate`. Content-based rather than commit-based on purpose: invalidating every attestation on every commit would make the mechanism unusable, and an unusable mechanism gets abandoned rather than obeyed.
